lead: Arizona looks dry, but monsoon storms, slab leaks and AC overflows put plenty of water where it does not belong. DryFlare helps homes and businesses from Phoenix to Tucson dry out quickly.
risk: monsoon flash floods, slab leaks and roof leaks during summer storms
risk_short: monsoon storms, slab leaks, AC leaks
why: The North American monsoon runs from mid-June through September. Storms build fast, drop an inch or more of rain in under an hour, and send water down washes and across streets. Hard desert soil sheds water instead of soaking it up, so it runs toward homes and pools against walls and patio doors. Flat roofs with parapets are common in the Phoenix area, and clogged scuppers turn a storm into a ceiling leak.

Indoors, hard water is the quiet problem. Mineral-heavy water wears out water heaters, supply lines and fittings early. Many homes sit on concrete slabs with copper or PEX lines underneath, and slab leaks can wet flooring for weeks before anyone notices. Arizona shares these desert issues with Nevada and New Mexico.
image_alt: Collapsed ceiling drywall after a roof leak during a summer storm
image_caption: A clogged roof drain during a monsoon storm can bring a ceiling down in minutes.
problems: Homes near washes in Phoenix, Mesa and Tucson
Homes and businesses with parapet roofs
tips: Clear roof scuppers and canales before monsoon season starts in June.
Replace water heater supply lines every few years; hard water speeds up wear.
Watch for warm spots on tile floors or a water bill that jumps; both can mean a slab leak.
Never drive or walk through a flooded wash.
insurance: Many Arizona policies cover sudden pipe bursts but not long, slow leaks, so a slab leak found early is more likely to be covered.

faq.q: Does monsoon flooding count as flood damage for insurance?
faq.a: Water that flows across the ground and into your home is usually treated as flood, which needs a separate flood policy. Rain that comes through a damaged roof is often covered by homeowners insurance. Ask your insurer which applies before cleanup begins.

areas: Calls also come from Yuma, Flagstaff, Prescott and Lake Havasu City.
